faq.a: Shakir is associated with the Arabic form شَاكِر, whose core sense is shakir; thankful, grateful.

faq.q: What is the origin of Shakir?
faq.a: Shakir is associated with Arabic. Shakir is Arabic شَاكِر (Shākir), the active participle of شَكَرَ, meaning 'thankful, grateful'.
Yes — the underlying form شَاكِر is Arabic.
Shakir can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Shakir should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root ش ك ر is Quranic, but Shākir is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Shakir mean in Urdu?

faq.q: What does Shakir mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Shakir is rendered شاکر and carries the sense شاکر، سپاسگزار.
A romanized syllable approximation is sha-kir. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Shakir?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Shakir, shakir. Script forms are شاکر, شَاكِر, शाकिर.

faq.q: Is Shakir a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
